issue.title: Block ID Picker: add block IDs to unidentified tasks (@route+ parent picker and Link picker)

task_type_fields.proposal:
Extend the Block ID Picker (bob-cli-2h) so a person can give an unidentified task a block ID from inside the picker, on two surfaces:

1. `@route+` / `@@route+` parent-task context: today these child-capture markers use the generic inline list. Route them into the same generic `CapturePicker*` card as `^` and `@route:` (browse the note's tasks grouped by heading, fuzzy filter), and when the chosen parent task has no `^block-id`, offer an "Add block ID" flow that proposes a Bob-suggested ID (reuse `capture_block_ids` suggestions and used-ID availability) and writes it.
2. Link picker (`@route:` as a whole item): today only tasks that already carry a block ID are linkable. Let the person pick an unidentified task and mint an ID for it in the same step.

Both need a new Bob contract: a completion/rewrite interface that adds an authored block ID to an existing task line atomically (`bob capture-task-id` already exists and may be the right primitive), plus Mac flow, fixtures, and tests in bob-mac-capture. Coordinate the contract across bob-cli and bob-mac-capture.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: The approved bob-cli-2h plan (plan:202609/mac_block_id_picker.md, Design decision 8) explicitly listed both the `@route+`/`@@route+` parent-task picker with its Add block ID flow and adding an ID to an unidentified task from the Link picker as out of scope, to be recorded as proposed follow-ups. They need a new write-side Bob contract, which that epic deliberately avoided.

issue.creation_reason: Recorded by the bob-cli-2h land agent from that epic's approved plan (Design decision 8), which named these picker surfaces as out-of-scope follow-ups.
